@servers.hub.colType.sameAsSourceJustification: French for the protocol/kind column is the identical word "Type": macOS Finder renders the "Kind" column as "Type" (LocalizableMerged.strings keys N224 / N169.35) and Apple's own profile detail panes ship "Type" -> "Type" (ManagedClient.app mcx/iChat profileDomainPlugin Localizable.loctable, key str_Detail_globalproxy_Type), macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, 2026-09-06.

@servers.sheet.protocolSmb.sameAsSourceJustification: Apple keeps the protocol acronym verbatim in French macOS: NetAuthAgent `Localizable.loctable` key `SMB_PASSWORD` -> "Mot de passe SMB", NetworkSettingsIntents `Localizable.loctable` key `SMB` -> "SMB" (macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, 2026-09-06). It is also on the catalog's own brand list.

@servers.sheet.protocolSftp.sameAsSourceJustification: Apple keeps the protocol acronym verbatim in French macOS: Sharing.appex `Localizable.loctable` key `SSH_INFO_GENERAL` -> "La connexion à distance autorise les utilisateurs d'autres ordinateurs à accéder à cet ordinateur via SSH et SFTP." (macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, 2026-09-06).

@servers.sheet.protocolWebdav.sameAsSourceJustification: Apple keeps the protocol name verbatim in French macOS: NetAuthAgent `Localizable.loctable` key `WEBDAV_PASSWORD` -> "Mot de passe WebDAV", WorkflowKit `Localizable.loctable` -> "serveurs SMB/CIFS, NFS, FTP (lecture seule) ou WebDAV" (macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, 2026-09-06). The shipped `servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer` already keeps it.

@servers.sheet.addressPlaceholder.sameAsSourceJustification: A literal example hostname, not prose: `nas` is the same abbreviation in French (the shipped `servers.hub.emptyMessage` writes "un Mac ou un NAS") and `.local` is the reserved mDNS suffix macOS itself shows (Finder `ConnectToWindow.strings` fr placeholder "Adresse du serveur" takes the same form). Translating it would print an address that does not resolve.

@servers.paneState.retryTotalMinutes.sameAsSourceJustification: French spells the unit exactly like English, singular and plural alike: « 1 minute », « 2 minutes ». The value IS translated (it carries French's own one/many/other categories, and the sibling seconds key reads « seconde »/« secondes »); there is simply no other French word for a minute.
